risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Cotton is the biggest component of cost and, being an agricultural produce, is subject to climatic and seasonal volatility; other input costs (power, fuel, logistics) are also rising regularly
- The textile industry is always subject to facing crisis in a cyclical way, requiring timely corrective and proactive action
- Competition from Bangladesh, Vietnam and China, which benefit from superior cost efficiencies and economies of scale, threatens margins and volumes
- Heavy dependence on exports makes the business vulnerable to global economic slowdowns, changing trade policies, currency fluctuations, and escalating US tariff barriers on imported goods
- The Russia-Ukraine conflict and the Middle East conflict have strained energy prices and global freight movement, weakening consumer sentiment in export destinations
- A major fire at the Company's factory premises in the previous year caused extensive damage to buildings, plant and machinery, furniture, equipment and inventories (including third-party job-work goods), temporarily impacting production; the Company also flags susceptibility to cyclones, earthquakes and other disasters causing shutdown, production cuts, project delays and supply chain hurdles
- Weak spending trends across both domestic and key international markets constrained volume growth in FY25-26
- Many segments of the Indian textile industry, particularly spinning and processing, suffer from technological obsolescence, leading to higher production costs and reduced competitiveness against low-cost imports
